channel.title: The Prototype
channel.description: Every week, The Prototype takes you inside the tech being built right now — the breakthroughs, the wild experiments, and the quiet revolutions that will shape the next decade. No hype, no jargon walls, just the amazing stuff explained straight. The future is already under construction. Come watch it get built.

item.title: The Prototype #5: Light on the Ocean Floor: The Cables That Carry the Internet
item.description: Ninety-nine percent of intercontinental internet traffic travels as light through glass threads on the ocean floor. Alden Isaac goes inside the undersea cable network: the Victorian dreamer who wired the Atlantic, the repair ships that fix four breaks a week, the Baltic sabotage gray zone, and why Meta is spending billions to lay its own private highway across the planet. Cover photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Music: "Deliberate Thought" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 3.0.

item.title: The Prototype #4: The Box That Shrank the World: The Truck Driver Who Rebuilt Global Trade
item.description: In March of twenty twenty-one, the Ever Given wedged itself into the Suez Canal and one stuck ship held up ten billion dollars a day in goods. All of it packed inside the same boring steel box. This is the story of the shipping container: the most important invention of the twentieth century, hiding in plain sight, invented by a truck driver who got tired of waiting at a dock. How a simple steel box rebuilt global trade, shrank the world, and put your phone, your shoes, and your coffee on a ship across the ocean. Cover photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Prototype #3: Carving Light: The Machine That Prints the Modern World
item.description: Every advanced chip on Earth is printed by a single machine built by a single Dutch company. Alden Isaac goes inside extreme ultraviolet lithography: vaporizing tin with lasers to make light that barely exists in nature, mirrors smoother than anything else on Earth, and the twenty-year bet the experts ranked dead last. Cover photo: ASML.

item.title: The Prototype #2: Your Phone Is Doing Relativity: The Hidden Genius of GPS
item.description: Your phone's blue dot is drawn by atomic clocks flying twelve thousand six hundred miles overhead, clocks deliberately set wrong at the factory to account for Einstein's relativity. In this episode of The Prototype, Alden Isaac goes inside GPS: the four-satellite math trick, the thirty-eight microsecond drift, the tragedy that opened it to the world, and how a military navigation system quietly became the heartbeat of modern civilization.

item.title: The Prototype #1: Bottling a Star: The Race to Put Fusion on the Grid
item.description: Fusion power has been thirty years away for sixty years. But in Everett, Washington, Helion Energy is building machines that smash rings of plasma together at one hundred fifty million degrees, and Microsoft already signed a contract to buy the electricity. In the premiere of The Prototype, Alden Isaac goes inside the race to bottle a star: Helion's fifty-megawatt Orion plant rising in Malaga, Washington, MIT spinoff Commonwealth Fusion's SPARC reactor nearing switch-on in Massachusetts, and the honest physics and engineering hurdles, from neutron-shredded walls to tritium shortages, standing between the workshop and the grid.
